read.thesis: Synchrony's Q1 2025 call shows credit improving (30+ DQ 4.52%, down 22bp) and a $2.5B buyback, but purchase volume fell 4% and ending receivables fell 2%, so the growth story is still stalled.

triggers.label: NCO guide cut to 5.8%-6.0%
triggers.quote: net charge-off guidance revised to 5.8%-6.0%, now within the long-term target of 5.5%-6%

triggers.label: NIM up 19bp to 14.74%
triggers.quote: Our first quarter net interest margin was 14.74% and increased 19 basis points compared to last year.

guidance.quote: We continue to expect net revenue between $15.2 million and $15.7 billion for the full year.
net charge-off guidance revised to 5.8%-6.0%, now within the long-term target of 5.5%-6%
we are maintaining our expectation of an efficiency ratio of between 31.5% to 32.5%.
we are maintaining our full year expectation of low single-digit growth in ending loan receivables.

guidance.metric: RSA as % of average loan receivables
guidance.quote: We now expect RSA as a percent of average loan receivables to be between 3.70% and 3.85%

guidance.metric: Liquid assets as % of total assets
guidance.quote: our liquid assets as a percent of total assets will average approximately 17% for the full year
Our target level, which we've shared is 11%.

red_flags.label: Purchase volume down 4%, receivables down 2%
red_flags.quote: Ending loan receivables decreased 2% to $100 billion in the first quarter due to lower purchase volume.

red_flags.label: Net charge-off rate above historical average
red_flags.quote: our net charge-off rate was 6.38% in the first quarter, an increase of 7 basis points from 6.31% in the prior year and 54 basis points above our historical average

evasions.quote: I actually do not care to comment. We're not calling it yet or a hypothetical for inflationary or -- I'm sorry, a recessionary environment.
It sounds like you're talking about a specific opportunity or to, Ryan, that I'm obviously not going to get into.
